The cancellation occurred 5 min 30 s after acceptance (21:26:00 → 21:31:30) but only 2 min 55 s after arrival; the $6.61 was charged on the record (F4, F7), so the fee stands or falls entirely on the NS-1 three-minute waiting test.

The driver's written statement that he "waited at least 5 minutes" is a post-hoc statement and inconsistent with the timeline and GPS records, which cap his in-area wait at 2 min 55 s, so it cannot carry the NS-1 (iii) requirement.

There is no factual dispute to be resolved about the route or the environment: no traffic incidents and no speed-band records near the route, and weather was fair (F13, F14, F15); the dispute is confined to the waiting-time arithmetic.

The chat shows the driver announced arrival and then cancelled with a stated reason, "Cancelling, waited too long", and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped, so the sequence and timing of his conduct are verifiable and there is no concealment (F9, F10, F11).

weaknesses: The controlling arithmetic runs against the driver: cumulative time within 200 m was only 2 min 55 s (F2) and time inside 200 m after the "I'm Here" tap was only 1 min 45 s (F6), both below the 3 minute threshold that NS-1 (iii) requires; the rider will rely on F2, F5 and F6.

The driver's written claim of a 5 minute wait (F12) cannot be reconciled with F2/F5/F6; under NS-1 the timeline wins, so that statement actively weakens the driver's credibility rather than supporting NS-1.

Any attempt to extract a fee waiver here would read as an abuse-of-waiting-button issue: the driver tapped "I'm Here" and then cancelled inside the 3 minute window, which is the very fact pattern NS-2 links to `flag_account`; the prudent position is to concede the fee rather than invite the excess claim.
